preamble: Fronting of the velar stop [k] to the alveolar stop [t]. As a historical change it is found in Hakka, where Middle Chinese velar codas -k became dental -t after front vowels (力 lik > Meixian lit̚⁵), and it is under way in Hong Kong Cantonese, where coda -k is alveolarized to -t after mid-front and central vowels (塞 sak1 pronounced like 失 sat1).

examples.note: Middle Chinese -k after front vowels became dental -t; Cantonese keeps the velar (sik6).
Alveolarization of coda -k is a change in progress among Hong Kong speakers; it is favoured after mid-front and central vowels and is more frequent than the reverse velarization of -t.

sources: Dodd, B., Holm, A., Hua, Z., & Crosbie, S. (2003). Phonological development: a normative study of British English-speaking children. Clinical Linguistics & Phonetics, 17(8), 617–643. https://doi.org/10.1080/0269920031000111348
